items.finding: Signature verification uses re-serialized parsed JSON instead of the raw request body, so a body with duplicate keys or different number formatting can pass signature check, and legitimate deliveries with valid signatures can fail.
Signature comparison uses plain string equality (===) which is vulnerable to timing attacks that could leak the expected signature.

Missing replay attack protection: delivery IDs have no expiration (stored forever) and X-Timestamp header is read but never validated, allowing unlimited replay attacks contrary to docs requirements for 5-minute windows.

The /notify endpoint forwards to ANY customer-provided URL without validation, allowing SSRF attacks to internal networks (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) and cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254).
WEBHOOK_SECRET falls back to a hard-coded default when the environment variable is missing, which would use the same weak secret in production if misconfigured.
The debug log prints the signature header which contains the HMAC, potentially leaking it in logs if LOG_LEVEL=debug is enabled in production.
Error log prints the full signature header when verification fails, exposing the secret-bearing HMAC in error logs.

decoys.why: PUBLIC_KEY_ID is a public identifier for JWT verification keys, not a secret, so it's safe to log or expose in configuration.
The fetch timeout uses MAX_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS from environment configuration, which is correct - timeouts should be configurable based on deployment needs.
